cars.generation: Original high-revving V8 RS 5 production-road family
cars.variant: 4.2 FSI quattro S tronic Coupe — September 2010 Japan introduction
cars.specification_market: Audi Japan production-road launch of September 13, 2010, using the original 4.2 FSI V8 coupe with seven-speed S tronic. The year identifies Japan introduction, not a US model-year designation. Primary Japan fields supply 331 kW at 8250 rpm, 430 Nm at 4000–6000 rpm, FSI direct injection, 12.3:1 compression, quattro and standard 265/35 R19 tyres. Displacement is retained as the nominal 4.2-litre class; an exact cc figure is not inferred. Optional 20-inch wheels, optional assistance/sunroof, carbon-ceramic brakes, raised speed limit, later facelift/cabriolet and racing-car data are not selected. Rear sport-differential availability is not generalized across markets.
cars.summary: The original RS 5 combined a high-revving naturally aspirated V8 with a significant evolution of quattro: the production debut of Audi’s self-locking crown-gear centre differential and wheel-selective torque vectoring. Its seven-speed dual-clutch drivetrain and dedicated wide-body A5-based coupe establish a substantive performance-engineering case. Count one original V8 RS 5 road family; facelifts, open-top versions, wheel choices and model years do not add entries.

sources.title: Crown gear differential — technology account, status 2011
sources.notes: Actual technical account read. Identifies debut in the RS 5 in early 2010, longitudinal front-engine application and nominal front/rear torque split of 40:60. Explains mechanically self-locking centre differential and brake-based wheel-selective torque vectoring; this is distinct from an active rear sport differential. Manufacturer handling superlatives and maximum torque-transfer percentages are not imported as test results.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The original RS 5 combined a high-revving naturally aspirated V8 with a significant evolution of quattro: the production debut of Audi’s self-locking crown-gear centre differential and wheel-selective torque vectoring. Its seven-speed dual-clutch drivetrain and dedicated wide-body A5-based coupe establish a substantive performance-engineering case. Count one original V8 RS 5 road family; facelifts, open-top versions, wheel choices and model years do not add entries.
